findings.title: T13’s samples-only fallback cannot produce residual offers
findings.description: T13 permits limiting selection to “store-recorded samples only” if no result-discovery surface exists. That surface does not currently exist: `capture.py#resolve_target` resolves one requested review, while `store.py#list_samples` returns only `SampleVerdict` records. Every such record is already sampled and therefore excluded by T13’s own unsampled-result definition, so this fallback necessarily produces zero offers. It cannot satisfy T13’s three-unsampled-results example or the slice’s non-empty-offer success criterion (`322-slice.calibration-to-threshold-feedback.md:269`). Replace the fallback with explicit persisted-review discovery work, reusing the existing identity/result-reference helpers and subtracting sampled results.

findings.title: T7’s precedence algorithm contradicts its required TIGHTEN behavior
findings.description: The numbered algorithm returns `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE` whenever `n < floor` before it reaches the `TIGHTEN` check. Consequently, a below-floor cell with a low match rate cannot return `TIGHTEN`, despite T7’s success criterion and T8 requiring exactly that result. The accompanying prose does not resolve the contradiction. Rewrite the decision order so the non-floor-gated tightening path is actually reachable, explicitly define its interaction with unversioned cells, and align T8 with that algorithm.

findings.title: The runtime-drawn-model limitation is missing from the recommendation-note requirements
findings.description: T9 requires only a general template/model pairing note. It omits the slice’s specific requirement that recommendations state the runtime-pool limitation: a threshold cannot track a model drawn at runtime, so the recommendation does not apply to that step (`322-slice.calibration-to-threshold-feedback.md:270`). T10 and T16 merely assert that the note is non-empty or that JSON round-trips, allowing this criterion to pass unnoticed. Add the limitation to the required note content and assert it in normal and `--json` output.

findings.title: Malformed judge-block coverage is claimed but neither implemented nor tested
findings.description: The Coverage Check at line 287 says malformed `judge:` blocks are exercised in T8, but T8 contains only registered- and unregistered-template cases. T7 likewise defines no malformed-value behavior. This matters because `resolve_thresholds` converts values with `float(...)`; a non-numeric floor raises `ValueError` rather than performing the warned fallback described by the slice’s failure-mode table. Specify the required handling and observable signal in T7, then add the malformed-block fixture and WARNING/flag assertion to T8.

findings.title: The offer-selection contract does not define how required outcomes are observed
findings.description: `select_residual_offers` returns only `list[OfferTarget]`, yet downstream tasks require three additional observability contracts: distinguishing lapsed from exhausted graduations, counting pruned targets, and naming skipped paths. T13 leaves the lapse signal optional and vague, while T14’s “skipped, counted” assertion has no defined count to inspect. Moreover, if candidates are discovered solely from currently existing review files, a deleted review cannot become a candidate in the first place. Define the candidate lifecycle and a concrete per-config outcome/logging contract—including lapse status and pruned count—before specifying these tests.

findings.title: Required empty-state CLI output is absent from T15 and T16
findings.description: The slice requires an empty recommendation report to print a “no evidence” line while still stating `floor_applied`, and an exhausted graduated config to produce an explanatory “no offers due” result. T15 specifies below-floor rendering only when a cell exists and lapse output only for `offers`; it does not specify either ordinary empty state. T16 correspondingly lacks both cases. Add the empty-store `recommend` and exhausted-config `offers` behavior and CLI tests.

findings.title: Config-key tests lack an oracle for the expected defaults
findings.description: T5 says all three keys must have descriptions and defaults, while T6 requires tests for their “correct” defaults, but neither the tasks nor the slice supplies the expected numeric values. A junior implementer cannot determine what those assertions should contain without inventing the answer. Name the three defaults—or identify an authoritative existing source—and use those values explicitly in T6.

findings.title: Task and commit granularity is excessive for this slice
findings.description: The breakdown creates eight separate implementation/test task pairs plus final validation, with a `**Commit**:` marker after every one of the 17 tasks. This produces test-only commits and places implementation commits such as T1 before their regression tests land, rather than consistently at tested working points. Fold each pair—T1/T2, T3/T4, T5/T6, T7/T8, T9/T10, T11/T12, T13/T14, and T15/T16—into one implementation task whose final steps are its tests. Retain T17 separately and place one commit after each completed, tested implementation task. This preserves the test-with pattern while cutting the task and commit overhead roughly in half.
